item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 221725
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Tue Sep 22 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Odalys, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of
Baja California, and on Hurricane Polo, located a few hundred miles
south-southeast of Manzanillo, Mexico.

Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (Former TD 15-E):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with the remnants of Tropical
Depression Fifteen-E, located several hundred miles southeast of
the Hawaiian Islands, have changed little in organization over the
past several hours. Environmental conditions are still expected to
be conducive for development, and a tropical depression is likely
to form during the next day or two while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward or northwestward. Heavy rains associated with
this system are forecast to spread over the southeastern Hawaiian
Islands starting on Wednesday and continuing into the weekend, and
interests in the Hawaiian Islands should continue to monitor the
progress of this system.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

South of the Gulf of Tehuantepec:
An area of low pressure is expected to form in the next few days to
the south of the Gulf of Tehuantepec. Afterwards, environmental
conditions should be favorable for gradual development, and a
tropical depression could form late this week or this weekend as
the system moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward. This
motion should keep it parallel to the coast of southern and
southwestern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Beven

THE OPEN EASTERN PACIFIC OCEAN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.1N 130.1W
ABOUT 1425 MI...2290 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...ENE OR 60 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Odalys was
located near latitude 15.1 North, longitude 130.1 West. Odalys is
moving toward the east-northeast near 3 mph (6 km/h) and this 
motion is expected to continue through the next couple of days, 
followed by a gradual turn to the northeast late this week.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 70 mph (110 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Additional strengthening is forecast, and Odalys
could become a hurricane later today or tonight.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 160 miles (260 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Sep 22 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 222043
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Odalys Discussion Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
200 PM PDT Tue Sep 22 2026

Deep convection was on a positive trend until recently, when the 
cloud tops started to warm based on the data from infrared satellite 
imagery, likely due to entering the diurnal convective minimum. The 
latest subjective TAFB Dvorak fix was T3.5/55 kt, which is the same 
as the last several cycles. The objective satellite intensity 
estimates from UW-CIMSS are in the range of 53-70 kt. Therefore, the 
initial intensity has been raised to 60 kt for this advisory.

The cyclone is currently moving east-northeastward, or 60/3 kt. This 
general motion is expected to persist as a trough that is moving 
over the eastern Pacific toward the western coast of the United 
States should deepen further. After this, the trough will become the 
main steering flow for Odalys resulting in an east-northeastward or 
northeastward motion for the next few days. After 72 h, the 
uncertainty in the track increases as potential interaction with 
Hurricane Polo could cause Odalys to slow down later in the forecast 
period. The current NHC track forecast is similar to the previous 
track with only a few minor adjustments and continues to be in good 
agreement with the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids.  

The cyclone is forecasted to be in an environment with weaker wind 
shear, plenty of mid-level moisture, and warm sea-surface 
temperatures, and this is expected to lead to additional 
intensification over the next few days. Thus, Odalys is forecast to 
become a hurricane tonight. After 48 h, Odalys will encounter a 
drier mid-level air mass and increased upper-level outflow from 
Hurricane Polo. The current NHC intensity guidance remains on the 
upper end of the model guidance, but close to the HCCA and GDMI 
forecast aids.

item.description:

884

BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Advisory Number   9
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
300 PM CST Tue Sep 22 2026
 
...POLO EXPECTED TO REMAIN AN EXTREMELY DANGEROUS CATEGORY 5
HURRICANE FOR THE NEXT COUPLE OF DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM CST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.6N 101.5W
ABOUT 215 MI...345 KM S OF ZIHUATANEJO MEXICO
ABOUT 355 MI...570 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...180 MPH...285 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...STATIONARY
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...892 MB...26.34 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Tecpan de Galeana to Punta San Telmo
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* West of Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere along the southwestern Mexico coast should
continue to monitor the progress of this system as additional
watches and warnings could be necessary tonight.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM CST (2100 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Polo was located by a
NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft near latitude 14.6 North, longitude
101.5 West.  Polo is nearly stationary, but a slow northwestward
motion is expected tonight followed by a generally
west-northwestward motion over the next couple of days.  On the
forecast track, the core of Polo is expected to be near the coast of
southwestern Mexico through the middle of this week, although it is
forecast to remain offshore.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 180 mph (285 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Polo is a category 5 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale. Some additional strengthening is possible
tonight, with fluctuations in strength possible Wednesday and
Wednesday night.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles
(150 km).
 
The minimum central pressure based on NOAA Hurricane Hunter
aircraft observations is 892 mb (26.34 inches). 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected within the warning
area along the coast of Mexico by early Wednesday.  Tropical storm
conditions are possible within the watch area along the coast of
Mexico by Thursday.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 3 to 6
inches, with isolated maximum totals up to 8 inches across coastal
portions of the Mexican states of Guerrero and Michoacán through
Thursday. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and
mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain. Rainfall of 2 to 4
inches is possible in coastal portions of Oaxaca, Colima, and
Jalisco through Thursday.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Polo are expected to affect portions of
the coast of southwestern Mexico during the next few days. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 600 PM CST.
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 8
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Tue Sep 22 2026 
113 
WTPZ42 KNHC 221455
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
900 AM CST Tue Sep 22 2026

Polo has a spectacular presentation on geostationary and microwave 
satellite imagery, with a small well-defined eye surrounded by a 
symmetrical area of very deep convection.  The upper-level outflow 
is quite prominent over all quadrants of the system and there are 
strong convective banding features surrounding the central dense 
overcast.  A Subjective Dvorak data T-number from TAFB just after 
1200 UTC was 7.0, corresponding to 140 kt, and assuming a little 
more strengthening since that time, the advisory intensity is set 
to 145 kt. Despite its great strength, Polo remains a relatively
small cyclone with its hurricane and tropical-storm-force winds
estimated to only extend about 30 and 80 n mi from the eye,
respectively.
 
The powerful hurricane appears to have stopped moving eastward, and 
it is now drifting northward at around 360/2 kt.  A deep-layer 
ridge is becoming established over Mexico.  This evolution of the 
steering pattern should result in Polo turning west-northwestward 
and beginning to move parallel, but fairly close to, the coast of 
Mexico over the next couple of days.  There is still uncertainty as 
to how close the hurricane will get to the coast, and some wind, 
rain, and surf impacts appear likely when Polo makes its closest 
approach.  A Tropical Storm Warning has been issued for a portion 
of the coast of Mexico and the Tropical Storm Watch has been 
extended westward.  Polo should begin to pull away from southwestern 
Mexico Thursday night and Friday as the ridge keeps the system on a 
west-northwestward to northwestward path.  The steering currents 
become more uncertain over the weekend when Polo reaches the western 
edge of the ridge and nears Tropical Storm Odalys to its west. 
However Polo is likely to slow down and move more northward around 
day 5.  Little change was made to the NHC track forecast, which lies 
on the northern side of the guidance envelope.
 
Polo should remain in an environment that is very  conducive for 
strengthening during next couple of days.  It should be noted that 
for these intense hurricanes, inner-core changes such as eyewall 
replacements are quite common.  These changes can lead to some 
fluctuations in intensity.  However, Polo is likely to remain a 
dangerous major hurricane through the forecast period.


Key Messages:
 
1. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo will impact coastal portions 
of southwest Mexico through Thursday.  This rainfall may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of 
steep terrain.
 
2. A Tropical Storm Warning is now in effect for portions of 
southwestern Mexico, and the Tropical Storm Watch has been extended 
westward along the coast.  Interests in these areas should closely 
monitor updates to the forecast.

item.title: Hurricane Polo Public Advisory Update Number
item.description:
Issued at 100 PM CST Tue Sep 22 2026 
855 
WTPZ62 KNHC 221940 CCA
TCUEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Tropical Cyclone Update
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
100 PM CST Tue Sep 22 2026

CORRECTED PRESSURE IN INCHES

...HURRICANE HUNTER AIRCRAFT FINDS POLO HAS STRENGTHENED EVEN 
MORE...
 
Reports from a NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft indicate that the 
maximum winds in Hurricane Polo have increased to near 180 mph 
(285 km/h) with higher gusts.  The minimum central pressure has 
dropped to 892 mb...26.34 inches.

Polo is nearly stationary but is expected to move generally 
west-northwestward over the next couple of days.

SUMMARY OF 100 PM CST...1900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.6N 101.5W
ABOUT 210 MI...335 KM S OF ZIHUATANEJO MEXICO
ABOUT 360 MI...575 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...180 MPH...285 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...STATIONARY
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...892 MB...26.34 INCHES
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch/Hagen
